subject: Game Theory
title: Altruistic Punishment
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Altruistic Punishment.

hook.text: Someone cuts in line. You could stay quiet—it barely costs you time. But you speak up anyway. Why?

buildup.text: Altruistic punishment means paying a cost to punish someone who violated a social norm, even without direct benefit.

discovery.text: Brain scans reveal the striatum lights up during punishment: enforcing fairness feels rewarding. It's satisfying.

twist.text: Cross-cultural studies show punishment norms vary wildly: some societies punish cooperators for making others look bad.

climax.text: Without altruistic punishers, cooperation collapses in experiments. They're the immune system of social groups.

punchline.text: Someone has to call out the cheaters.

quiz.question: Why is altruistic punishment important for cooperation?
options: It deters free riding and upholds norms
